text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Unidentified gunmen shot dead 21 worshippers, including 10 children between ages of 10 to 15, in a dawn attack on a mosque in Pakistan's central city of Multan.
- A leader of Shi'ite Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan was shot dead in the town of Bahawalpur, 95 km (60 miles) south of Multan.

- President Farooq Leghari has sent messages to National Assembly (Lower House) speaker and Senate (upper house) chairman proposing amendments in laws aimed at empowering the President to consult the opposition leader, Supreme Court chief justice and the prime minister in appointing judges for corruption cases.

- Eight people were injured when police fired tear gas shells and bullets in Larkana to disperse protesters mourning the death of Murtaza Bhutto, who was killed in Karachi on Friday in firing between his bodyguards and the police.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto said even after the killing of Murtaza Bhutto the enemies of the Bhuttos were still conspiring to eliminate other family members.

- The government has redesigned a package to seek resumption of $600 million standby loan and reach agreement on a new Extended Structural Adjustment Facility programme with the IMF. The package promises imposition of tax on agricultural income and slashing non-development expenses.
- The International Finance Corporation sees no political instability in Pakistan and has plans to continue offering financial support specially to the private sector.
- The European Union has threatened to impose anti-dumping duty on bed linen exports from Pakistan.
- Pakistan exported rice worth $155,000 to Japan during January-June 1996 compared to rice exports worth $3,000 in the same period last year, Japan External Trade Organisation said.
